items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
Secrecy applies in the mortal world among the lowest people
items.inference: This teaching should be carefully hidden from unworthy people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of people.

items.question: To whom may this teaching legitimately be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Only a previously accomplished person tested for one year is a fit recipient.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being identified
It is the fifth chapter
items.inference: This marks the end of the fifth chapter in the Candradvīpa recension.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of Kaula been understood?
premises: The speaker claims knowledge
The knowledge concerns the determination of Kaula
This knowledge arose by the grace of the lord of Kaulas
items.inference: The determination of Kaula is known through the lord's grace.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in the teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is unknown
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The speaker asks for a full account of where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality being described?
premises: The subject is identified as supreme
It is partless and eternal
It is free from disease and stainless
items.inference: The ultimate reality is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from affliction, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in terms of haṃsa and śakti?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That supreme soul is identified as haṃsa
It is also characterized as the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is equated with haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.
uncertainties: The exact sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is interpretively compressed.
items.plain_english: That soul which is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
It is situated somewhere
Its location is in all living beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The subject leaves the body
This departure is the condition described
At that moment it is called supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, the soul is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and perceived according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes down through tradition
The goddess is addressed as witness
items.inference: The teaching is received aurally through an unbroken traditional lineage.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What effect is attributed to merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing alone is emphasized
The fair-faced goddess is addressed
items.inference: Even mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as efficacious.
uncertainties: The specific result of hearing is completed in the following verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, simply heard,

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice continues for six months
The practitioner cultivates a renunciant state
That state is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a bondage-free renunciant condition.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer to an ochre robe or a renunciant condition.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What benefits follow for the practitioner freed from all diseases?
premises: The practitioner becomes free from all diseases
Association with yogis is mentioned
Union with them is attained
items.inference: Freedom from disease culminates in union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching about the soul's practice has now been communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: A teaching has been told
Its content is the practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the addressed recipient
items.inference: The exposition of the soul's practice has been completed for Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: What kind of resolved recipient is fit to receive this teaching?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: The teaching should be given to a fully prepared person of firm resolve.
uncertainties: The case shift between genitive and locative is unusual in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and whose mind is firmly resolved.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
It originates from the yoginīs
Giving it is explicitly prohibited
items.inference: The sacred Kaula essence of yoginī origin must not be disclosed to the unfit.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body from ignorance to purity is being claimed?
premises: The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
A present change is asserted
The body is now declared pure
items.inference: The speaker claims her body has become pure, freed from ignorance's veil.
uncertainties: deham appears in accusative form but functions as subject in this transmitted reading.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish to hear
The topic concerns time
The desired teaching is the auspicious overcoming of time
items.inference: The speaker now seeks instruction on the auspicious conquest of time.
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ can mean deception or overcoming; context favors overcoming.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can truly be destroyed?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
There is no doubt in the matter
The explanation shows how death is destroyed
items.inference: The teaching confidently asserts a method by which death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you without doubt how death is destroyed.

items.question: What paradoxical condition affects even the wise at the point of nectar?
premises: The context involves the tip of nectar
There is contact with the essence
Even a wise person experiences burning
items.inference: Even the wise may feel a burning sensation at the nectar's point.
uncertainties: The precise yogic referent of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one, at the tip of nectar, is burned by the tip of that essence.

items.question: What yogic technique involving breath at the palate is prescribed?
premises: Attention is placed at the root of tongue and palate
The breath is directed there
One should drink the breath slowly
items.inference: The prescribed practice is to slowly draw in the breath at the palate's root.
items.plain_english: Placing the breath at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink it in.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this technique for one year?
premises: The practice is performed for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: A year of sustained practice leads to the destruction of old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to poison is claimed for one accomplished in this practice?
premises: The person may be bitten by great serpents
Poison would normally enter the body
In this case poison does not enter the body
items.inference: The accomplished practitioner remains immune to serpent poison.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
